intention: Register a workflow for the concept-piece class, and give press_office the state + history it cannot journal without one. concept-piece is the ONE node class in CairnCommons/node_classes/ with no workflow_versions key (code-seam has v1+v2, skill has v1, host-seam and operational-driver are registered) — so no workflow string naming it can parse, no crossing can be emitted, and every concept-piece is structurally unable to journal. press_office/ is the visible cost: charter and proofs/ beside its code, and no state.json, no history.json.
why: Law 5 says intent, its voyage, and its proofs share an address. press_office has two of the three: a charter and a proofs/ directory, and no state.json, no history.json. The lived symptom belongs to the next reader who opens press_office/ and asks a plain question — 'when did §3 of the brief last change, and why?' Today the only answers are `git log`, which records bytes and not crossings, and a paragraph in proofs/PROOF.md that someone REMEMBERED to write. Both 2026-08-05 revisions happened to get recorded that way. The next one is recorded only if the next author remembers too, which is policy, not physics (Law 4). The structural cause sits one level up and is not press_office's fault: concept-piece.json carries no workflow_versions, so no workflow string naming that class can parse at all. Every concept-piece the system will ever cast inherits the same silence.

falsifier: FALSIFIER, in two teeth that must both be green. (a) A workflow string 'concept-piece@v1: …' PARSES and CONFORMS through cairn/tools/base/transitions.py — the same load_class_def + _conform the emit chokepoint and the /sorted door already run, so no new validator is written and 'zero new machinery' is itself checkable. (b) press_office/state.json and history.json exist and are COMPILED, not authored: the antiproof is that the proof must red on a hand-written state.json. A proof that merely asserts the two files exist is the coin-toss-green this corpus has already met — file-existence cannot fail once a file is written. distinctions_recorded: SUPERSESSION vs THE VOYAGE — press_office's charter says how_it_learns: 'By supersession, not in-place update.' That rule's why is about the DOCUMENT'S CONTENT: a superseded claim stays readable, so a piece is replaced rather than edited under itself (Law 7). This ticket's why is about CROSSINGS: which ones a node made and when. A journal of crossings does not edit content — it is what makes supersession legible, since 'superseded by' is an event with a date. They compose; no conflict.

THE ROAD IS NOT THE JUDGE — concept-piece's prove_gate is a human quorum signature and code-seam's is the tester; skills/sorted/SKILL.md warns explicitly not to collapse those hands. Registering a workflow path for concept-piece changes WHICH CROSSINGS EXIST, not who proves them. PROVEME for a concept-piece remains the signature gate described in press_office/proofs/PROOF.md.

A CONCEPT-PIECE NODE IS A DOCUMENT, AND ONE COMPONENT HOLDS MANY VOYAGES — read off disk, not assumed: concept-piece.json's members_so_far names a file path. press_office/ is the component; its three documents are three nodes. CLAUDE.md already settles the addressing ('a ticket's voyage freezes here when it proves out'), so three voyages in one history.json is the normal case, not an addressing problem to solve.
